images.caption:
Green Mosque of Bursa, Turkey, 2017.
Green Mosque (Turkish: Yeşil Camii, "Yeşil Mosque"), also known as Mosque of Sultan Mehmed I, is a part of the larger complex (a külliye) located on the east side of Bursa, Turkey, the former capital of the Ottoman Turks before they captured Constantinople in 1453. The complex consists of a mosque, türbe, madrasah, kitchen and bath.

images.filename: Bursa Green Mosque Loge Decoration at arch in 2018 7814.jpg
images.caption: I do not know which lower loge I photographed most. Both are spectacular, with cuerda seca work and green tiles, and decoration along the insides and front sides of the arch at their entrance. I do not know their function, but think they may have been mahfili, spots where a chanter or a group of them might reside. As usual light conditions and my equipment varied over the years.
images.alt: I do not know which lower loge I photographed most.
